doc.title: John Budd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [transcript only]

title: Favorite bands of the 1930s, lyrics, and meeting Johnny Mercer and Condon's band
summary: Coon-Sanders and McKinney's Cotton Pickers, his love of lyrics, and the postwar Condon's lineup.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Who were some of your big favorites in the 30’s?

I knew more favorites than individuals. I suppose that Coon Sanders, I loved to hear them play. McKinney’s Cotton Pickers was a jazz band. There’s a new one now in Detroit but this was the old one. I just knew the name, I never saw them. “It’s Tight Like That” was a © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -8-

jazz tune and “Rosetta” and numbers like that. And that was McKinney’s Cotton Pickers, not Coon Sanders. The Coon Sanders, they had a tune called “Deep Henderson” I’d never heard before, and I think there’s: Flamin’ mamie/The sure fire vamp/The hottest baby in town/She’s a heart scorcher/She loves torture/She loves to burn ‘em down. I remember those lyrics and that’s 70 years ago, but they made an impression evidently. I thought that people who write lyrics are bright, and that’s led my interest into them. Of the ones that I’ve met, the one that I am most fond of is Johnny Mercer. I met him by accident. Many of my things have been by accident, not by me looking for something. I became friendly with a bunch at Eddie Condon’s place. This was after the war and I knew most of them at the time when the band was Gene Schrader played the piano, Cutty Cutshaw played the trombone, Wild Bill Davis on the trumpet, and Walter Page on the bass and Eddie Condon on the guitar.
